scope.description: Whole IfcOpenShell library and tooling breadth across model reading, authoring, geometry, validation, schema versions and utilities.
scope.denominator: IFC reading and writing across schemas, entity and property families, geometry processing, units and placement, validation, classification, cost and scheduling utilities and conversion tools.

coverage.rationale: One IFC4 wall schedule with a small property and quantity subset exercises a tiny part of the library. Geometry, other classes, schemas and authoring are outside the integration.

scope.description: Bounded GUID-linked IfcWall property and quantity schedule with explicit precedence, missingness and units, handed to a typed workbook.
scope.denominator: User intent and domain decisions within this one wall-schedule workflow; other classes, geometry and model authoring are outside this denominator.

abstraction.rationale: Authors name property and quantity columns and policies and receive a verified typed schedule without writing native code. They still decide which quantities are meaningful, supply the exact set names and judge whether the stored values are right; the workflow is a hypothesis without demonstrated customer demand.

limitations: One ASCII IFC4 file, plain IfcWall only, IfcPropertySingleValue and three plain-SI quantity kinds; no geometry, other classes, schema versions, materials, relationships or authoring. Numbers and #ids anywhere in the file are held to a declared lexical budget (40 mantissa digits, exponent magnitude 400, 10 id digits) and must be valid STEP INTEGER or REAL text; larger exact decimals are unsupported. Unselected entities and geometry are unassessed.

Agreement between IfcOpenShell and the independent reader shows both read the same stated values; it does not show the model, its quantities or the schedule are right for the building. The workflow is a hypothesis without demonstrated customer demand.
Subjective source-contract assessment; no exhaustive API denominator supports these percentages.
